item.title: Food and Tradition on Display at the B.C. Club Bake Sale — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Becky Byerly-Adams This month we explore the Icelanders who settled in British Columbia. Before the holiday season approaches the Icelandic Canadian Club of British Columbia (ICCBC) in Burnaby held their Bake Sale. But it was much more than that. Becky gives us a first hand account of what she experienced attending the Bake Sale. Food can be much more than sustenance. It is a means of preserving one's cultural heritage and identity. When over 16,500 Icelanders emigrated to North America...

item.description: By Linda Brandson Coates (I558622) This month's review of North American settlements addresses British Columbia, the most western province in Canada. It is here where W.D. As an accomplished author, poet and teacher, we are grateful for his time with us as a guest of the Icelandic Roots Book Club. item.title: ICELANDERS OF SPRING RIDGE — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Fred Bjarnason Victoria, British Columbia, was a very different place when Icelanders began to settle here in 1883 than it is now. The city followed the waterfront along the inner harbour, extending inland only about four or five blocks. The Icelanders began to settle in an area east of the main city known as Spring Ridge, now the neighbour of Fernwood.
